title: Payment-History Extension Months on a Patient Payment Plan Modification
content:
**Patient Financial Services tier table — extension months from the payment record of a Patient Payment Plan**

When the installment and term of a Patient Payment Plan are modified, the plan's payment record gives history months toward the extension: they follow the returned-payment fees booked on installments within the last 12 months — two or more give 1 month, exactly one gives 2 months, and none gives the tier's maximum term extension. The extension months of a modification are never more than the tier's maximum term extension in total.

Returned-payment fees are placed by the due date of the installment they were booked on; an installment lies within the last 12 months when fewer than 12 whole calendar months separate its due date from the handling date.

## History months by tier

| Tier | Maximum term extension (months) | None in the last 12 months | Exactly one | Two or more |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Short-Term 3-Month Payment Plan | 0 | 0 | 2 | 1 |
| Standard 6-Month Payment Plan | 0 | 0 | 2 | 1 |
| Extended 10-Month Payment Plan | 2 | 2 | 2 | 1 |
| Long-Term 12-Month Payment Plan | 2 | 2 | 2 | 1 |
| Large-Balance 18-Month Payment Plan | 3 | 3 | 2 | 1 |
| Hardship 24-Month Payment Plan | 6 | 6 | 2 | 1 |

## Hypothetical readings

- A Large-Balance 18-Month Payment Plan with no returned-payment fee on installments due in the last 12 months: 3 history months.
- The same plan with one such fee: 2 history months; with three: 1.
- A fee booked on an installment due 13 months before the handling date is not counted.
